title: CWE-209: raw exception text leaked to unauthenticated clients via detail=str(e)
description: Routes wrap business logic in `except Exception as e: raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(e))` at lead.py:16, calculator.py:14 and contact.py:12. Any unexpected exception - SQLAlchemy/DB constraint violations, Pydantic coercion errors surfaced from deeper layers, path/OS errors - is echoed verbatim to the client, including module paths, file paths, SQL snippet fragments and library internals. Frontend amplifies the exposure: services/api.js:14 extracts `error.response.data.detail` into the thrown Error message, and Hero/CTA/Contact/Calculator forms render that message into the DOM. No auth anywhere, so any internet client can probe inputs to harvest internals (recon for further attacks).
impact: Information disclosure of internal error details (paths, framework internals, DB errors) to unauthenticated remote clients; facilitates targeted follow-up attacks.
mitigation: Replace blanket `except Exception` + str(e) with validation-aware handling and a centralized error mapping that returns generic messages and logs full details server-side only; cap/neutralize the frontend interceptor to never surface raw detail strings.
